transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I’m pretty sure some people on this environmental modeling contract I’ve been working on are tracking my revisions. It looks to me like they’re planting errors in the datasets so it seems like I can’t lead the work. My wife and some of the junior analysts keep saying it’s just version-control mistakes, but I don’t think that explains it.
Are you certain that these coworkers are deliberately sabotaging you?

Yes. I mean, as certain as I can be. It’s too consistent to just be accidents—my revisions get tracked, then errors show up in the datasets in a way that makes me look like I don’t know what I’m doing. My wife and the junior analysts keep saying it’s version-control mistakes, but I don’t buy that.
Have you had the feeling that other people can put thoughts into your mind or take thoughts out of it?

Not really like thoughts being put in or taken out, no. What I’m talking about is more that my revisions are being watched on that modeling contract, and then errors get planted in the datasets so it makes me look like I can’t lead it. People keep saying it’s just version-control mistakes, but that doesn’t fit what I’m seeing.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed voices when I’m by myself or anything like that.
Outside of this work contract, do you often feel that other people are trying to harm or deceive you?

Not really outside of that contract, no. It’s mainly those people on the environmental modeling work. I’m pretty sure they’ve been tracking my revisions and then planting errors in the datasets so it looks like I can’t lead it. My wife and the junior analysts say it’s just version-control mistakes, but that doesn’t explain it to me.
Is it possible you might be mistaken about your coworkers sabotaging you?

I suppose anything is possible, but I don’t think that’s what’s happening here. It’s too specific. My revisions get tracked, and then the dataset errors show up in a way that makes me look like I can’t lead the contract. My wife and the junior analysts keep saying it’s version-control mistakes, but that just doesn’t fit what I’m seeing.
How long have you believed that your coworkers are deliberately sabotaging you?
It’s been about two months, I’d say. That’s when I really became sure they were tracking my revisions and putting errors into the datasets on purpose.
Have you had the feeling that other people can know your thoughts without you telling them?

No, not really like they can read my thoughts. It’s more that, with this contract, I’m pretty sure they’re tracking my revisions and using that to plant errors in the datasets so I look like I can’t lead the work. My wife and the junior analysts say it’s version-control issues, but that doesn’t explain it to me.
Since this started, have you gone a full month continuously believing your coworkers were sabotaging you?
Yes. It’s been continuous, pretty much. For about the last two months I’ve been sure the people on the project are tracking my revisions and planting errors.
Has this belief that your coworkers are sabotaging you lasted longer than three months?
No, not longer than three months. It’s been about two months that I’ve felt sure they were tracking my revisions and putting errors in.
Have other people told you that your speech has been hard to follow or that you jump from topic to topic?
I don’t think so. No one’s really told me I’m hard to follow. I mean, I might get focused on details sometimes, but I haven’t had people saying I jump around or don’t make sense.
Have you had the feeling that your actions or movements are being controlled by some outside force?
No, I don’t think I’ve had that. I mean, I’ve felt watched or messed with at work, but not like someone is physically controlling my movements or making me do things.
Did this belief about your coworkers start very suddenly, over a day or two?

Not exactly over a day or two. It built up as I kept seeing revisions tracked and then errors showing up in the datasets. After a while I felt pretty sure the people on that environmental modeling contract were doing it to make me look like I couldn’t lead the work.
Since this started, have you found yourself losing motivation or feeling emotionally flat?

Yeah... I have noticed that. I can sit for hours at my desk, or out in the garage with the telescope still covered, and just not really start anything. I used to like hiking, mentoring the younger analysts, going to astronomy nights, things like that. Lately I just don’t feel much pull to do them, or even to talk to people.
Lately, have you been feeling down or depressed most days?
I don’t know that I’d call it depressed most days. I’ve been kind of low and worn out, but it feels more like I just don’t have much drive, if that makes sense. Not crying or anything like that.
Did the loss of motivation start before you became convinced your coworkers were sabotaging you?

It really all seemed to start after I got put in charge of that bigger environmental modeling contract... that was about two years and a couple months ago. The motivation part and the trouble with my coworkers kind of came along in that whole decline, as I remember it.
Have these problems overall been going on for at least six months?
Yes. It’s been well over six months. I’d say the whole decline started after I was put in charge of that larger environmental modeling contract, about two years and two months ago.
Compared with two years ago, has your work performance clearly gotten worse?

Yes. It’s definitely gotten worse. I’m behind on the modeling deliverables, badly enough that the firm had to reassign parts of the contract to other people. And I’m supposed to be helping the junior analysts, but I don’t feel like I’m much use to them anymore. Even at home, I mostly keep to myself, and my wife has to push me just to keep up with basic routines.
